working_papers.title: LIPE: Latent Interview Protocols Engineer
working_papers.summary: Introduces a method and software tool for recovering latent interview protocols from interview corpora by clustering interviewer utterances into protocol questions using semantic embeddings, and modeling typical question sequences as directed graphs. The approach enables researchers to reverse-engineer semi-structured interview designs and retrieve responses by inferred question type.

working_papers.title: A Genealogy of Philosophical Framing in Methodological Disputes
working_papers.summary: Presents a genealogical analysis of how philosophical framing entered and evolved within qualitative–quantitative methodological debates. The paper traces how different actors mobilized philosophical concepts in distinct ways across historical moments, and analyzes these uses through the lens of social-epistemic theories, including echo chambers and willful ignorance, to understand how methodological disagreements persist and stabilize.

working_papers.title: HIPR: Hierarchical Propositions for Computer-Assisted Text Analysis
working_papers.summary: Introduces a method and software tool for recovering propositions from text using a semantically rich formal model. The paper proposes hierarchical propositions as a representation that captures a broader range of semantic content than prior approaches while enabling entailment relations between propositions. This structure allows propositions and proposition counts to function as analytic features, extending beyond word-based representations and enabling more sophisticated search and exploration of large text corpora.

working_papers.title: Computer-Assisted Text Analysis: History and a General Framework
working_papers.summary: Examines the historical development of computer-assisted text analysis methods across multiple fields and proposes a general framework for conducting such analyses. The framework is informed by established approaches to qualitative text analysis and aims to clarify the role of the researcher at each stage of analysis, specifying how computational tools can assist interpretive work. The paper argues that this approach can help establish computer-assisted text analysis as a robust methodological tradition in the social sciences, rather than as a hybrid or compromise between qualitative and quantitative methods.

working_papers.title: The Epistemic Goals of Research
working_papers.summary: Argues that persistent methodological disputes are partly driven by the absence of a shared account of the epistemic goals of research. The paper critiques traditional conceptions of truth as a research goal while also rejecting arbitrariness because that would undermine the possibility of epistemic authority. It seeks to articulate an intermediate account of epistemic goals that can serve as a common reference point for evaluating and adjudicating methodological disagreements across research traditions.
